## Solution

The vector field is
$$V = x\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z} + y\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x}.$$

Equipping $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the standard Euclidean metric
$$g = dx\otimes dx + dy\otimes dy + dz\otimes dz,$$
the dual (flat) one-form $V^\flat$ is defined by the musical isomorphism
$$V^\flat = g(V,\,\cdot\,).$$

Writing $V$ in the coordinate basis with all three components explicit:
$$V = y\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x} + 0\,\frac{\partial}{\partial y} + x\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z}.$$

By linearity of $g$ and using $g\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i},\,\cdot\right) = dx^i$:
$$V^\flat = y\,g\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x},\,\cdot\right) + 0\,g\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial y},\,\cdot\right) + x\,g\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial z},\,\cdot\right)$$
$$= y\,dx + 0\,dy + x\,dz.$$

Therefore the dual one-form field is

$$\boxed{V^\flat = y\,dx + x\,dz.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE

For $V = y \frac{\partial}{\partial x} + 0 \frac{\partial}{\partial y} + x \frac{\partial}{\partial z}$:

$g(V, \cdot) = y \, g(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}, \cdot) + 0 \, g(\frac{\partial}{\partial y}, \cdot) + x \, g(\frac{\partial}{\partial z}, \cdot)$

$= y \, dx + 0 \, dy + x \, dz$

$= y \, dx + x \, dz$
